issues.description: Method getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor(): the problem statement UML (problem_statement.md) declares getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor(): double, the solution implementation (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java) declares public int getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor() and performs integer division, while the template (template_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java) instructs students to implement the method as specified in the UML. This inconsistency causes loss of fractional results (integer division) and confuses students about the expected return type and signature — tests or graders expecting a double result or signature may fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type consistent with the UML: change the method signature to public double getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor() in the solution (and document in the template) and compute using floating-point division, e.g. return (double) getTotalNumberOfStudents() / getNumberOfTutors();. Also consider handling the case where numberOfTutors is zero (for example return 0.0 or document the expected behavior) to avoid division-by-zero surprises.
